title: What's the weather like?
goal: Talk about the weather and the seasons, then compare two things with *daha* and *en*.
bekal: answering *hava nasıl* for all four seasons
comparing with the pattern *X, Y'den daha ...*

dialogs.title: Dialogue — Kar yağıyor
dialogs.intro: Early December. Budi stands at the window, looking out over the whitening rooftops of Kadıköy. Emre comes in with two glasses of tea.

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.id: Yes! There's no snow at all in Indonesia.

lines.speaker: Emre:
lines.text: Hiç mi? Peki hava nasıl orada?
lines.id: None at all? So what's the weather like there?
lines.literal: at-all question? well weather how there?

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Her zaman sıcak. Otuz derece, bazen daha fazla.
lines.id: Always hot. Thirty degrees, sometimes more.
lines.literal: every time hot. thirty degree, sometimes more much.

lines.speaker: Emre:
lines.text: Yazın İstanbul da sıcak olur ama Jakarta kadar değil.
lines.id: Istanbul gets hot in summer too, but not like Jakarta.
lines.literal: in-summer Istanbul too hot becomes but Jakarta as-much not.

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.id: How many degrees is it now?

lines.speaker: Emre:
lines.text: Sıfır. Yarın daha soğuk olacak, eksi üç.
lines.id: Zero. Tomorrow it'll be colder, minus three.
lines.literal: zero. tomorrow more cold will-be, minus three.

lines.speaker: Emre:
lines.text: Merak etme. Kalın bir mont al, bir de atkı.
lines.id: Don't worry. Get a thick coat, and a scarf too.
lines.literal: worry don't-do. thick a coat take, one also scarf.

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.id: What's the coldest month in Turkey?

lines.speaker: Emre:
lines.text: Ocak. Ama Erzurum'da kış İstanbul'dan çok daha zor.
lines.id: January. But in Erzurum the winter is much harder than in Istanbul.
lines.literal: January. but Erzurum-in winter Istanbul-from very more hard.

notes: **Kar yağıyor, yağmur yağıyor.** Turkish uses one verb for everything that falls from the sky: *yağmak*. Snow, rain and hail all *yağar*, and the thing itself is named first.

**Yazın means "in summer".** The four seasons have their own adverb forms, with *-ın*: *yazın*, *kışın*, *ilkbaharda*, *sonbaharda*. The first two are leftovers of an old suffix that survives in just a handful of words.
**Kadar means "as much as".** *Jakarta kadar sıcak değil* = "not as hot as Jakarta". To compare equals, Turkish uses *kadar*; for differences, *-den daha*.
**Donarım ben** uses the aorist from unit 13 for something that hasn't happened yet — a playful Turkish exaggeration, like "I'll freeze to death!" in English.

blocks.text: The suffix *-lı* found in almost every weather word means "with" or "having": *yağmur-lu* (rainy), *kar-lı* (snowy), *rüzgâr-lı* (windy) — much like English *-y*. Its opposite is *-sız* ("without"), and both are covered fully in the next unit.

blocks.title: Turkey isn't one climate
items: The Mediterranean coast (Antalya, Alanya) is warm all year. The Black Sea coast (Trabzon, Rize) is the wettest place in Turkey — rain almost every month, and that's where the tea gardens are.
Eastern Anatolia (Erzurum, Kars) can drop to minus thirty in January. If someone asks *Türkiye'de hava nasıl?*, the honest answer is always: *Nerede?*

blocks.text: Turkish never changes the adjective itself. For "more", it puts the word **daha** in front; for "most", the word **en**. The thing being compared with takes the *-den* suffix.

head: Pattern
Example
English
rows: Ankara is as big as Istanbul.
Ankara isn't as big as Istanbul.

blocks.text: To strengthen it, put *çok* before *daha*: *çok daha soğuk* (much colder). To weaken it: *biraz daha soğuk* (a little colder).

head: Türkçe
English
rows: Daha ucuz bir şey var mı?

blocks.title: Bence, sence, ona göre
items: "In my opinion" is *bence* — the suffix *-ce* attached to a pronoun: *bence*, *sence*, *bizce*. The same suffix forms language names: *Türk-çe*, *İngiliz-ce*, *Endonezce*.
For a third person, a different form is used: *ona göre* (according to him/her), *Ayşe'ye göre* (according to Ayşe).

blocks.text: *Ayakkabı* is literally "foot container" — *ayak* (foot) + *kap* (container) + *-ı*. Turkish is full of compounds like this: *buzdolabı* (fridge, "ice cupboard"), *bilgisayar* (computer, "information counter"), *çamaşır makinesi* (washing machine).

exercises.prompt: Answer in one sentence as indicated.
Compare using *-den daha*. The first word is the subject.

items: Ankara isn't as big as Istanbul.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in the right order.

answers: Hava güneşli. — Yağmur yağıyor. — Hava çok soğuk. — Yirmi beş derece. — Eksi üç derece. — Kar yağıyor.
İstanbul, Ankara'dan daha büyük. — Yaz, kıştan daha sıcak. — Türkçe, Arapçadan daha kolay. — Bu şal, o şaldan daha pahalı. — Otobüs, taksiden daha ucuz. — Bugün, dünden daha soğuk.
Hava nasıl? — Bugün dünden daha soğuk. — En soğuk ay hangisi? — Daha ucuz bir şey var mı? — Bence Türkçe daha kolay. — Ankara, İstanbul kadar büyük değil.
Hava nasıl? — Bugün kar yağıyor. — Yarın daha soğuk olacak. — En soğuk ay hangisi? — İstanbul, Jakarta kadar sıcak değil. — Bence Türkçe daha kolay.
